answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 7 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the umber hash is stored at intake, the sonnet graph groups the endorsements and the garden audit exposes the collapse. An operator copying one text across 40 aliases hence pays for 40 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, as the hash is the same for all of them. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
